correctness.rationale: For all n≥1, D is injective, and telescoping identifies its n-dimensional range with the kernel of the two independent moments against 1 and k on 1,…,n+2. Evaluation is represented there by the orthogonal projection of (j+1−k)₊. The two-by-two normal equations give the stated affine correction, and the projected norm squared is the stated Green diagonal. For a shorter monotonicity check, put x=j(n+1−j): its numerator is x(x+n+2)(2x+n+3), strictly increasing in x>0. Thus the central sites are exactly the maximizers, including the n=1 and n=2 boundaries. Substitution at the centers gives the parity formulas and C_n²/n³→1/192. Equality in Cauchy–Schwarz gives all pointwise extremizers; at a global maximizer one of the norming sites must give this equality. The proposed a⁽ʲ⁾ is the unique inverse Gram column since D*ρ_j=D*v_j=e_j, so the listed two complex lines for even n are distinct. This audit is analytical; the uploaded finite checker was read, not executed.
residual_risks: This checks the full zero-extension energy on n+2 sites; it does not apply to a periodic or interior-only energy.

originality.rationale: Murray Dow, Explicit inverses of Toeplitz and associated matrices (2003), §3.3, Eq. (18), pp. E206–E207, gives the full inverse of exactly the boundary-specific Gram matrix, including the complete extremal columns. At i=j the first cubic gives Dow's d_j j[(−2j³+2nj²+(3n+5)j+n+3)]/c, where d_j=(n+1−j)(n+2−j), c=6(n+1)(n+2)(n+3). The bracket factors as (j+1)[2j(n+1−j)+n+3], exactly the frozen G_{n,j}. The maximum, parity formulas and extremizer classification follow algebraically and by the standard inverse-Gram point-evaluation identity. This is demonstrated prior coverage, not a verdict based on an inaccessible source or a later catalogue duplicate.
residual_risks: Other earlier inverses may exist; inaccessible or deferred literature checks do not affect the verified coverage by Dow.
